title: The Book That Plays Back
description: A print gamebook you play against: make a move, turn to the page it sends you to, and the book has already replied — every answer precomputed by minimax with a trap-maximising tie-break. Five games (tic-tac-toe, hexapawn, notakto, nim, twenty-one), a history-of-machines foot timeline, essays on the MENACE matchbox learner and the Sprague–Grundy theorem, a glossary, a cut-out matchbox kit, and a certificate. Generated deterministically by a short Python program (book.py) from random seed 43, typeset with Forme, compiled with XeLaTeX; rebuilds byte-identically from source. Print edition ISBN 978-65-02-14290-5. The book (text and figures) is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0; the code is MIT.
